cohort: Pregnant women scheduled for a cesarean section
finding: Women undergoing humanized cesarean sections reported higher satisfaction, lower anxiety, reduced postoperative pain requiring less analgesia, and their babies had greater weight gain at 10 days postpartum, while no significant differences were found in exclusive breastfeeding rates at 10 days or blood counts between the groups.
mod_finding: Natural cesarean sections were associated with higher exclusive breastfeeding rates at 3 and 6 months compared to conventional cesarean sections.
